title: The Minimal Dimension of Entangled-Noise Advantage
authors: Xiao-Ke Wang, Zi-Yuan Liu, Ming-Yang Li, Shengjun Wu, Zeng-Bing Chen
abstract: Can entangled noise erase entanglement more efficiently than separable noise? Standard robustness restricts the added noise to separable states; generalized robustness allows any state. We prove that the two costs coincide for every two-qubit state and give an explicit full-rank qubit--qutrit state with a strict gap. Positivity under partial transpose (PPT) characterizes separability in both dimensions, so the boundary is not caused by a failure of the PPT criterion. Instead, product-vector geometry permits a rank-one bridge between the two-qubit dual optimizations and supplies a two-dimensional completely entangled subspace for the qubit--qutrit separation. Local isometric embeddings complete the finite-dimensional bipartite classification, also for any fixed multipartite cut. Combined with known three-qubit separation, the result classifies universal equality relative to full separability in all finite multipartite systems.
summary: This theoretical paper investigates the difference between two measures of entanglement robustness: standard (separable noise) and generalized (any noise). It proves that for two-qubit systems, these two measures are always equal, but demonstrates a strict inequality for the qubit-qutrit system. This work provides a comprehensive classification of when entangled noise offers a quantifiable advantage over separable noise in finite quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper compares two measures of entanglement robustness—standard ($R_s$) and generalized ($R_g$)—to determine if entangled noise can erase entanglement more efficiently than separable noise.
main_result: The equality $R_s(ho) = R_g(ho)$ holds only for two-qubit states in bipartite systems, but a strict gap is found for the qubit-qutrit system, indicating an advantage for entangled noise.
method: The analysis uses semidefinite programming (SDP) formulations, optimization over noise operators, and geometric arguments involving product-vector spaces to classify the equality boundaries.
model_or_system: The study focuses on bipartite quantum states ($\mathcal{C}^m \otimes \mathcal{C}^n$) and general finite multipartite systems, analyzing robustness relative to full separability.
key_observables: The two robustness measures, $R_s(ho)$ and $R_g(ho)$, and the gap $R_s(ho) - R_g(ho)$.
important_parameters: The dimensions of the subsystems ($m, n$) and the number of parties ($N$) in the multipartite setting.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the PPT criterion characterizes separability in both robustness settings, and the results are for single-copy robustness, not asymptotic tasks.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing the problem in bipartite systems, proving equality for $2 \otimes 2$, then constructing a counterexample for $2 \otimes 3$, and finally generalizing the classification to arbitrary finite multipartite systems.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous, quantitative classification of when entanglement resources are equally protected against different types of noise, which is fundamental for understanding noise resilience in quantum communication protocols.
